"In June, we determined that IJAMEA - the Japanese department of anomalous research - was developing an eigenweapon codenamed Oyamitsumi."

From my perspective on things, IJAMEA of years after 1945 is effectively remnants who keep using the brandname of 'IJAMEA'. In terms of resources, they can easily run the gauntlet from being fully stocked with anomalous technology to just the guy armed with only a pocket knife in a dark alley.

It is clear that Oyamitsumi is the former.

item.content:encoded:
I'm conflicted about this. While I liked the subject matter and the ideas here, I would prefer reading about these events outside of an orientation format in a way that is less of an infodump. However, this is a good rundown on eigenweapons for those who need it with cool imagery, and a nice setup for later tales.

I'm upvoting, but my issues with this still stand.

item.title: Showtime
item.content:encoded:
+ On the next episode
- Stay tuned

She snarled at them, a wild animal, driven mad by the Worm's essence; by a fractional distillation of the power, of the age, of the immensity of the Worm. The animal thrashed outwards; the essence of the Worm lashed outwards and twisted. The men and women trying to save the world were warped: their spines contorted and their eyes plunged inwards, stealing brain matter to make more eyes and their lungs started muttering under their own breaths as their skulls rotated counterclockwise to reality.

Part 3 of 4.

The theme for this episode is Phoenix Rising, by Lost Years.

This has been almost a year in development. It is probably garbage, and I will hopefully never write another orientation tale again. There will be one more episode in this season. Stay tuned.
